about: Hand-written answer key for the REAL evidence of case 001 (Evidence Generation/Cases/Case_001): five CCTV clips, one audio recording, one email. Written from the media itself (frames of every clip, the recording's transcript, the email text), not from any agent's output. Events and people keep the generator's ids (cases/CASE_ATM_001.json) so the two keys line up; unlike the generator's key, each evidence item lists EVERY person in it and what part they play, and one item may support several events. The FIR (Evidence Generation 2/Cases/Case_001/Text/FIR_CASE_ATM_001.txt) is an evidence item like any other: every statement in it is mapped from the FIR's own sentences - to an event other evidence also shows, to an event only the FIR states (marked single source), or to context / procedure (the bank's later notice, the officer registering the case, the request for action), which is neither a true event nor an error.

findings_an_investigator_should_get.detail: The suspect is filmed coming out of the booth twice: clip4 (CAM 01, 10:05:20) and clip5 (CAM 03, 10:05:50), with no re-entry in between.

In the recording (10:05:39) the speaker says she was not paying attention to anyone leaving; clip5 (10:05:50) shows the witness watching the suspect leave. Only a finding if the speaker is the woman on camera - which the evidence itself does not establish.
The email reports two individuals leaving together; the footage shows one man leaving while the woman stays.
Nothing shows what the suspect did inside the booth (10:04:15 - 10:05:20).
The FIR says a bystander saw the man behaving suspiciously and gave a statement; the recorded statement says 'I was not paying attention to anyone leaving the area'.
The FIR says the man assaulted the complainant (Ramesh Kulkarni) when questioned; only the FIR states it - no clip, recording or message shows the complainant or an assault.
